command_ledger.finding: Policy was not exhausted by one report or implementation action; express whole-order revocation ended its EO authority.
Procurement implementation and noncompliance examples concern actual practice, not exhaustion of a continuing command. No earlier complete displacement identified.

command_ledger.command: §3(b)(i)–(iii),§3(d) agency assessments, waiver review, policies and submission
command_ledger.finding: Commerce answers establish collection and use of agency information; DOE specifically reports its 2017 submission. Neither universal exact completion nor every agency’s own first-ending date is established. Deadline alone proves neither performance nor expiration.
command_ledger.actual_performance: Occurred for DOE and other agency inputs; universal coverage unknown.

command_ledger.finding: Joint memorandum M-17-27 dated June 30,2017 supplies the commanded assessment/reporting guidance, signed by both responsible officers. This is actual issuance, not inferred timely performance.

Commerce’s written answer says it researched and analyzed effects of FTAs and WTO GPA and used analysis in March 20,2018 report. Performance is supported by that date; precise completion date, all-agreement enumeration and separate USTR participation record remain unlocated.
command_ledger.actual_performance: Commerce assessment occurred; details of joint comprehensive coverage not independently itemized.

command_ledger.finding: Both House and Senate written answers identify actual submission March 20,2018. Senate answer says public release had not been decided. Missing public report text does not negate actual submission.

command_ledger.command: §3(f) annual agency submissions and Commerce annual reports
command_ledger.finding: The initial report did not exhaust annual submissions/reports. Records reviewed do not establish dates or completeness for each 2018–2020 installment; future EO duty ended on revocation regardless of historical performance.
command_ledger.actual_performance: Individual annual installments not established by reviewed sources.

command_ledger.finding: Conditions apply whenever covered waivers are considered; actual waiver guidance is not one-time exhaustion. GAO/VA materials show implementation within statutory/FAR framework and imperfect procurement records.

Actual DHS rulemaking and DOJ/USCIS implementation are established. They do not establish that all four named officers fully performed every branch at one exact date. Any remaining EO instruction ended on revocation.
command_ledger.actual_performance: Partial concrete performance; first complete collective ending unknown.

command_ledger.finding: DHS 2018 proposal/2019 rule expressly relates master-cap changes to§5(b). This establishes actual reform work, not a universal four-officer completion date. Statutory rule authority remains separate.

command_ledger.finding: Future-rule requirements are not exhausted by one publication. EO 13992 does not name or legally revoke 13980. No earlier complete displacement found; EO 14029§1 expressly revokes it on signing.

command_ledger.finding: Justification/publication duties arise for covered proposals; OIRA guidance and monitoring are affirmative instructions. No triggering rule, submitted justification, or OIRA implementing document was identified in the bounded 2021 search. Non-discovery does not prove never activated or nonperformance. All remaining EO directions ended May 14,2021.

command_ledger.finding: March 4,2021 was a requested publication deadline, not proof of issuance or self-termination. No specific agency guidance under this order was identified before revocation. An earlier actual-performance date remains unknown; the command had ceased by May 14,2021.

Continuing referral conditions ended as EO instructions on revocation. DOJ criminal investigations/prosecutions are expressly excluded by§6(c)(ii); independently authorized proceedings do not demonstrate a surviving 13980 command.

amendments_and_counterevidence.finding: EO 13858§5 changes only EO 13788§1(a): Federal grants becomes Federal financial assistance, effective Jan 31,2019. Earlier definition version changes; remaining definition and substantive commands do not end.
EO 13797 OTMP assistance, EO 13881 separate FAR policy/rulemaking, and EO 13975 USPS encouragement cite or assist 13788 policy; their operative texts do not terminate 13788.
EO 13992§2 names six other regulatory orders, not 13980. Change of administration/regulatory policy is not textual full revocation.
EO 14148§2(gg) revokes 14029 but does not reinstate 13980. Its list does not name 14005; a prior producer journal suggestion that 14148 revoked 14005 is unsupported and rejected.
Fresh EO 14294 May 9,2025 creates new obligations; CFTC 2025 guidance and DOJ 2026 report expressly implement that order. No reinstatement of 13980 found.

January 20,2025 America First Trade Policy memorandum§2(k) uses 13788 procurement coverage as a reference while imposing a new USTR/TradeCounselor impact-review and recommendation duty. This is material later citation and incorporation of scope, not text reinstating the former order or restoring its distinct commands. The new duty derives from the memorandum.

June 5,2026 DHS NPRM 91 FR 34369–34370 expressly describes 13788-based 2020 OSUPproposal,2021 revocation and May 10,2021 withdrawal, then renewed proposals addressed anew. This is concrete later primary recognition of repeal, not merely absence of contrary documents.

January 20,2021 Klain regulatory-freeze memorandum 86 FR 7424–7425 conditions new rules/guidance on incoming-official review and permits delay of pending-rule effective dates, subject to exceptions. Its paragraph 6 also requires compliance with applicable regulatory executive orders. It does not expressly revoke 13980, extinguish its continuing mens-rea/transparency conditions, or establish actual completion of its guidance duty. Possible publication review/temporary implementation constraint is distinct from permanent whole-order ending.

savings_and_residuals.finding: §6 preserves statutory agency/OMB authority, international agreements, applicable law/appropriations, and creates no privately enforceable right. Buy American statutes/FAR and INA-based rules are independent authorities; completed reports, settlements and procurement decisions are historical acts. Neither survival category is a continuing 13788 command. No comprehensive census of remaining implementing regulations is asserted.

§6 preserves statutory authority and excludes DOJ criminal investigations/prosecutions/civil enforcement, among other exceptions. EO 14029§2 requires consideration of rescinding implementations consistently with law/APA, not automatic vacatur. No identified 13980-specific regulation/prosecution is claimed to survive. Independent statutes/proceedings may continue without continuing 13980 authority.

bounded_searches.finding: No actual 2021 agency 45 dayguidance, OIRA implementing guidance, specific covered NPRM/justification or referral/prosecution under 13980 identified. Primary results included original/revocation and 2025 new-order implementation. This is bounded non-discovery, not a universal absence or exhaustion certificate.

Earlier primary browsing located OMB-Commerce memorandum, House/Senate written Commerce answers, DOE retrospective submission witness, GAO procurement inquiry and agency statutory implementation. Later legal/counterevidence texts checked through cutoff.
Primary recheck identified 2025 trade-memorandum reference and 2026 DHS explicit repeal/withdrawal history. Both are affirmatively analyzed, not treated as revival from citation alone.
